note: Inclusive/exclusive comparisons in src/engine that no test holds.
A boundary is 'held' when flipping <= to < (or >= to >) makes a test fail. On
2026-08-30 forty-seven of sixty-eight were not held. This list should SHRINK,
and on 2026-08-31 it did, three times: nine, then seven, then ten, leaving
twenty-one. Only a NEW entry fails the check -- the backlog is a backlog, not a
monthly alarm, and an alarm that always fires is not an alarm.
Held on 2026-08-31 by tests/engine/statutoryThresholds.test.ts (the lines a
statute draws) and tests/engine/engineThresholds.test.ts (the ones this codebase
drew for itself), then planThresholds and financeThresholds in a third pass:
benefits 367       the 100% FPL floor for the premium tax credit -- at exactly
the poverty line you are eligible, and `>` would leave that
household with nothing offered at all
benefits 223       SNAP's minimum benefit, which floors households of one AND
two; `<` would quietly pay a couple $21 instead of $24
benefits 283/304   the open-ended top ACA band (fplHigh: null) at exactly its
floor -- unreachable from the shipped 2026 table, so it took
an ARPA-shaped fixture to reach the branch at all
socialSecurityTax  the $25,000 / $32,000 / $34,000 provisional-income bases.
67 and 70       Both readings compute the same dollars at the base; only the
TIER differs, and the tier is what the tile prints
iraDeduction       the phase-out endpoints. Same shape: the same dollars either
109 and 112     way, but 'partial' beside an undiminished deduction, or
beside no deduction, is a contradiction the reader inherits
garnishment 145    which of the two federal limits binds at the exact crossover
($290 weekly). The module commits in a comment to giving the
tie to the protected floor; nothing held it to that
dueDates 21 (>=)   the LOWER half of MLK Day's third-Monday window. When
January 15 is a Monday it IS the third Monday, so the Q4
1040-ES payment moves to the 16th. Flipped, the engine
names a due date on a day the IRS is closed
amt 76             an AMT base of exactly zero. Flipped, it falls through to
the 85% band where `0 >= 0 * 0.85` is TRUE, so a filer with
no exposure at all is told they might owe AMT
amt 80             the 'maybe' band at exactly 85% of regular tax
cliffs 213         the sweep needing exactly MAX_POINTS: `stepWidened` flips,
and the chart says it was widened when it was not
cliffs 321/325     a resource dip of exactly CLIFF_NOISE_FLOOR ($1): a drop of
$1, or a plateau reported at depth $0
cliffs 359         the top of the swept range, which is the point a household
is about to walk into
plan 181/276/364   every 'are you there yet' comparison in the goal plan. The
plan's advice is a dollar figure, so anyone who follows it
lands EXACTLY on the target -- and the flipped reading
hands that person an active step reading 'set aside $0.00'
plan 223           a debt at exactly the high-cost rate the user chose. The
config's own comment says 'at or above'
plan 349           essential expenses of exactly zero. Flipped, the target is
$0, any net worth clears it, and the plan tells someone who
has entered nothing that work is already optional
finance 311        a mortgage term of exactly zero years, which is one
comparison away from dividing the principal by zero
finance 486        the 31st of the month in the cash-flow timeline. Flipped,
the day is dropped in silence and the month ends richer
than it will
finance 867        landing exactly on the coast-FIRE number -- the Downshift
Point, where saving becomes optional
finance 1142       the last age of a retirement drawdown, so 'lasts to 90' is
answered from a projection that actually reached 90
finance 1345       clearing a transferred balance in the FINAL month of the
intro window, which is inside it
TRIAGED AS REDUNDANT. For these the branch and its `else` compute the same
observable answer at the boundary, so no test can distinguish the readings.
They are branches, not decisions. They stay listed rather than deleted, because
'nothing depends on this' is a finding the next reader should not have to
re-derive -- and because a branch can stop being redundant (amt 67 would, the
day its second term gained a constant).
Verified by a test that pins the identity making it redundant:
amt 67             `baseNum <= breakpoint`: at the breakpoint the two-rate
formula reduces to the one-rate formula. A split point
educationCredits   the phase-out endpoints, which -- unlike iraDeduction's --
56 and 57       set no status the reader sees, and the interpolation in the
else branch yields exactly 1 and exactly 0 at those points
educationCredits   the AOTC/LLC tie-break. With the statutory ratios the AOTC
77              is STRICTLY larger wherever either is positive (100% of the
first $2,000 against 20% of the same dollars), so the
tie-break never runs on a tie
Analysed as redundant, not yet pinned by a test (a reading, so recorded as one):
finance 135/1263   the 'a payment that cannot cover the interest never retires
the debt' guard, in debtPayoff and in the phased balance-
transfer simulation. Both loops end with `if (bal > 0)
return null`, so at exactly equal payment and interest the
answer is null either way -- the early return is a FAST
PATH, saving 1,200 iterations of no-op decimal math, not a
decision. Pinned by financeThresholds anyway: the contract
it expresses is the one that matters
finance 330        `n <= 0` in loanPrincipalFromPayment, which looks like its
sibling at 311 and is not: 311 DIVIDES by n and overflows
without the guard, while 330 multiplies by (1 - (1+r)^-0)
= 0 and returns zero either way
finance 653/736    a spend at exactly the deductible, and a loan paid off in
exactly its term
benefits 166       `size <= top`: past the table's top the fallback adds the
per-person amount times (size - top), which is zero AT top
benefits 352       `pct >= 100 && !acaCovered(pct)`: the shipped table covers
from 0% FPL, so !acaCovered only fires above 400% FPL,
where the `>= 100` guard is already trivially true
iraDeduction 86    roundPartial's `amount <= 0` guard, unreachable: a MAGI at
or above the range's high end returns before it
fafsa 71 and 76    the same short-circuit shape as educationCredits, on the
AAI assessment's zero point and its bracket lower bounds
brackets 20        `taxable <= 0`: the loop's own first comparison breaks at
zero anyway
brackets 202/231   the Oregon federal-tax-deduction phase-out and the Arkansas
and Connecticut recapture ramps: linear ramps whose endpoint
short-circuit agrees with the interpolation, exactly as the
education credits do
costBasis 46       `remaining <= 0`: the next lot takes zero shares and the
`take > 0` guard drops it
taxMoves 89        the $3,000 capital-loss offset limit, where both arms of the
ternary are the same value at equality
UNHOLDABLE THROUGH THE PUBLIC API, which is a different verdict again:
dueDates 21 (<=)   the UPPER half of the MLK window. It guards a fourth or
fifth January Monday from being called the holiday, and no
1040-ES date falls on January 21, so nothing observable
turns on it. Holding it would mean exporting `isMlkDay` to
test an internal, which is a worse trade than leaving a
line on this list
The rest are untriaged, and are a mix of real statutory lines and defensive
guards. Deciding which is which is a reading, and a list that pre-filtered by
someone's reading would hide the one they got wrong.
